summary: This section explains that documents and information required by the law must be submitted and registered on time with the proper fee. If a company misses the deadline for specific documents under section 92 or 137, it can still file them later by paying an additional fee of at least one hundred rupees per day. Failing to file on time also makes the company and responsible officers liable for other penalties and punishments mentioned in the Act.
points: Documents, facts, or information must be submitted, filed, registered, or recorded within the time specified in the relevant law provision.
A prescribed fee must be paid when submitting or registering documents.
Documents required under section 92 or 137 can be filed after their original deadline by paying an additional fee of at least one hundred rupees per day.
Different additional fee amounts can be set for different classes of companies.
Failing to submit or register documents on time leads to penalties or punishments for the company and its officers in default, along with the required fees.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited was required to file certain annual documents under section 92 by a specific deadline. Unfortunately, the company missed this date. To fix the issue, the managers submitted the documents after the deadline had passed. Because they filed late, the company had to pay the standard fee plus an additional fee of at least one hundred rupees for every day of delay. Even after paying this extra money, the company and its responsible officers still faced other potential penalties and punishments allowed under the law for missing the original deadline.

terms.meaning: Decided or specified by the rules or authorities.
Company officers who are responsible for the failure or violation of the law.

watch: Paying the additional late fee does not protect the company or its officers from other legal penalties for missing the deadline.
